item.title: Mercosur deal to officially be signed off on today
item.description: The controversial Mercosur deal will be officially signed off on today. The agreement opens up trade between the European Union and South America. Ireland voted against it, but it was approved by the majority of EU member states. Speaking in Rio de Janeiro last night, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said it's an "historic" move that will be prosperous for all: Advertisement

item.title: Local senator announces step back from X
item.description: A local senator has announced that he is taking a step back from the social media platform X. This follows controversy on the platform as the AI tool, Grok, has faced criticism for allowing users to create naked and sexualised images of women and children. X has announced that Grok's "nudification" mode has been blocked in Ireland. Senator Joe O'Reilly has deactivated his account, as he sees Grok as dehumanising to women and children. item.title: Tommy Kelly
item.description: Tommy Kelly late of Phibsboro, Dublin 7, and formerly of 4 Carn Gardens, Clones, Co. Monaghan Tommy Kelly passed away on Friday 16th January, peacefully in Cavan General Hospital, surrounded by his family. Predeceased by his loving wife Nancy, her sister Phyllis, his brother Stan, his sisters; Maida, Pauline, Noreen and Iris. Sadly missed by his brothers Brendan and Leo, his nieces and nephews, including John and Adrian Kelly, the Cooke family in Clones, the Kelly families in the UK, USA and Aus

item.title: Gardaí reissue appeal for information following Virginia burglary
item.description: Gardai in Co Cavan have reissued their appeal for information following a burglary in Virginia. An investigation was launched as a result of the incident which occurred on the 5th of December. According to Gardai, the burglary took place in Lakelands Apartments on the Dublin Road between the hours of 8:45am and 3pm. The homeowner returned to find an apartment door damaged. item.description: Cathaoirleach of the Ballybay-Clones MD, Sinead Flynn has raised her concerns over the level of housing planned for the area. item.title: A3/N54 near Clones closed after lorry overturns
item.description: The A3/N54 Cavan Road has been closed this morning following a road traffic incident involving an overturned lorry. The incident occurred on the stretch of the A3 heading towards Clones. Advertisement Diversions are currently in place and motorists are being advised to seek alternative routes at this time.

item.title: Monaghan moving in the right direction
item.description: Monaghan reached the Bank of Ireland Dr Mc Kenna cup final with a 2 point win over Tyrone on Wednesday past in Paric Gratten Inniskeen. It has been the perfect start to 2026 for Gabriel Bannigans side as they also registered wins over Fermanagh and Tyrone. Our reporter Sean Mc Caffrey spoke to former Monaghan county player Dessie Mone, getting his thoughts on how the competition has gone so far We will have live coverage of that final on Saturday Sport from 5pm Advertisement

item.title: Donegal down Monaghan to Dr. McKenna Cup
item.description: Donegal claimed a 12th Dr. McKenna Cup with a convincing 12-point win over Monaghan. Jim McGuinness side controlled the game, particularly in the second-half, having led 1-7 to six points at half-time. Stephen Mooney opened the scoring with a fifth minute free. However, it was the only time Monaghan led in the game. Shea Malone responded with a Donegal goal a minute later. Hugh McFadden added a point two minutes later to move Donegal three clear. item.title: Fog warning issued for Cavan tonight
item.description: A status yellow warning has been issued for Cavan and 15 counties. The fog warning has been issued for Carlow, Kildare, Kilkenny, Laois, Longford, Meath, Offaly, Westmeath, Cavan, Clare, Limerick, Tipperary, Waterford, Galway, Leitrim, and Roscommon. Areas of dense fog or freezing fog possible, leading to impaired visibility and hazardous travelling conditions. Advertisement The warning is valid from 9pm tonight and will run until 10am tomorrow.
